statement: For an optimal control problem with dynamics $\frac{\mathrm{d}x(t)}{\mathrm{d}t} = f(t, x(t), u(t))$, initial condition $x(t_0) = x_0$, and objective functional $J(t_0, x_0; u) = \int_{t_0}^{t_1} I(t, x(t), u(t))\,\mathrm{d}t + \phi(x(t_1))$ maximized over admissible controls $u \in U[t_0, t_1]$, the value function $V(t_0, x_0)$ is defined as the supremum of the objective function over the set of admissible controls: $V(t_0, x_0) = \sup_{u \in U[t_0, t_1]} J(t_0, x_0; u) = J(t_0, x_0; u^*)$, where $(x^*, u^*)$ is the optimal state and control trajectory pair, with terminal boundary condition $V(t_1, x(t_1)) = \phi(x(t_1))$.

symbols.meaning: Value function representing the optimal payoff (or cost-to-go) from state $x$ at time $t$ over $[t, t_1]$
Set of admissible controls (Lebesgue measurable functions from $[t_0, t_1]$ to a prescribed subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$)
Optimal pair of state and control trajectories
Costate variable vector $\partial V(t, x)/\partial x$
Hamiltonian function $I(t, x, u) + \lambda(t) f(t, x, u)$

properties.why: At the terminal time $t_1$, the running integral vanishes and the remaining payoff is solely the scrap value

properties.property: Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) PDE: If $V(t, x)$ is continuously differentiable, it satisfies $-\frac{\partial V(t,x)}{\partial t} = \max_u \left\{ I(t, x, u) + \frac{\partial V(t,x)}{\partial x} f(t, x, u) \right\} = \max_u H(t, x, u, \lambda)$
properties.why: Derived from Bellman's principle of optimality applied to the remaining problem from state $x(t)$

properties.property: Costate equation recovery: Identifying $\lambda(t) = \frac{\partial V(t, x)}{\partial x}$, differentiating the HJB equation with respect to $x$ yields $-\dot{\lambda}(t) = \frac{\partial I}{\partial x} + \lambda(t) \frac{\partial f(x)}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial H}{\partial x}$
properties.why: The total time derivative of $\lambda(t)$ matches the spatial derivative of the HJB equation

properties.property: Viscosity solution: The value function is the unique viscosity solution to the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation
properties.why: Accounts for cases where the value function fails to be continuously differentiable

properties.property: Lyapunov function: In online closed-loop approximate optimal control, the value function acts as a Lyapunov function
properties.why: Establishes global asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system

assumptions.assumption: Admissible controls $u$ are Lebesgue measurable functions mapping $[t_0, t_1]$ into a prescribed subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$
assumptions.breaks_when: Controls are non-measurable or fail to satisfy prescribed control constraints

assumptions.assumption: Continuous differentiability of $V(t, x)$ for the classical HJB formulation
assumptions.breaks_when: The value function develops non-differentiable points (kinks), requiring weak or viscosity solutions

failure_modes.signature: Partial derivatives $\frac{\partial V}{\partial t}$ or $\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}$ do not exist everywhere
failure_modes.cause: Optimal control problems often produce value functions with non-smooth boundaries or shocks, violating the assumption of continuous differentiability

failure_modes.signature: No admissible control achieves $V(t_0, x_0) = J(t_0, x_0; u^*)$
failure_modes.cause: The admissible control space $U[t_0, t_1]$ is non-compact or the running payoff/dynamics fail lower/upper semi-continuity requirements
